## Problem

Change 1996 (`02f71da097`, RP-05 S5) added two steps to `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml`
that invoke repository files, **without the if-present guard this repo mandates for exactly
this case**:

```yaml
- name: parser-derived docs are byte-current on the lean wheel
  run: |
    /tmp/clean/bin/python scripts/gen_cli_help.py --check
    /tmp/clean/bin/python scripts/gen_cli_reference.py --check

- name: clean-wheel distribution + every-help-form byte contract (portable pytest)
  run: |
    /tmp/clean/bin/python -m pytest ... tests/interfaces/contracts/test_cli_registry_distribution.py -rs
```

`tests/interfaces/contracts/test_cli_registry_distribution.py` was **created by that same
commit** (141 lines, new file).

## Mechanism

Gerrit's verify job takes the workflow **DEFINITION** from the target branch but checks out the
**CHANGE'S** tree. So a step added on `main` runs against every open change whose base predates
it. The test file is absent in those trees, pytest collects nothing, and exits 4:

```
collected 0 items
============================ no tests ran in 0.01s ============================
##[error]Process completed with exit code 4.
```

That is a `Verified -1` caused by the gate, not by the change under review.

## Measured blast radius — 3 open changes, all innocent

Failing the identical job at 34-47s, none of them touching the CLI registry or packaging:

| change | subject |
|---|---|
| 1997 | Resolve access-check client seam at call time |
| 1998 | Stop absent-string child oracles failing open |
| 1999 | Fail closed on stale KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS rows |

`main` itself is green: "Optional-Dependency Isolation (mirror)" and the full "Test Suite
(mirror)" both succeeded, and the whole job reproduces clean locally against `origin/main` in a
no-extras venv (`rebar --help` exit 0; agents-absent assertion OK; 17 passed).

## The remedy already exists in this repo

This hazard is documented (ticket `ee2a`, bug `1909-c1a7-9f20-440f`) and every other
script-invoking gate step carries the guard. From `_build-and-test.yml`:

```yaml
- name: comment-hygiene gate
  run: |
    if [ ! -f scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py ]; then
      echo "not in checked-out tree (change predates the gate) — skipping;" \
           "the gate re-enforces on rebase and on every post-merge change"
      exit 0
    fi
    python scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py
```

The Verified-gate parity gate and the raw-git-write gate use the same shape. The two new
optionality steps are the outliers.

## Why this is a defect and not a nuisance

A gate that reds a change for a reason unrelated to the change **trains reviewers to discount
the gate**. That is the failure mode `recheck` discipline exists to prevent: once a `-1` can
mean "your base is old", every `-1` becomes ambiguous, and the two-vote gate loses its meaning
as evidence. The cost is already visible — three unrelated changes, each of whose authors must
otherwise investigate a failure that is not theirs.

## Scope

Add the established if-present guard to the two new steps. Match the existing wording so the
skip is self-explaining.

Explicitly OUT of scope: changing what the steps check, weakening either `--check`, or altering
the distribution contract. The steps are correct; only their unguarded invocation is wrong.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Both new steps skip with an explanatory message when their target file is absent from the
      checked-out tree, matching the existing guard wording — verified by a test or a CI dry-run
      against a tree lacking the file
- [x] Both steps still run and still fail on a tree that DOES contain the file, so the guard
      cannot be satisfied by simply never running — verified by a positive case
- [x] A change based on pre-`02f71da097` `main` passes the optionality lane — verified against
      one of 1997/1998/1999 before their rebase, or an equivalent reconstruction
